meta.title: Leo's Revision Notes: Mixing and Changing
meta.textType: functional: a school science text with headings, on the class blog

paragraphs: Posted by Leo. Hello, Explorers! Today is Monday, March eighth, and the English test is finished. Now I am at my desk at home, and I am writing my notes for the science test on Wednesday. On my desk there are a notebook, a glass of water, a small bowl of salt, and a spoon. Teacher Kim reads every post before it goes online, so these notes are checked by her. My notes have three headings.

What is a mixture? Chemistry is the science of materials and how they change. The word mixture comes from mix, so a mixture is something that is mixed. Salt and water make a mixture. Perfume is also a mixture of oil, water, and the smell of flowers. Perfume and salty water are similar, because both are mixtures. Various things can be mixed, such as sand and rice, or paint and water. Even air is a mixture, but we cannot see it. Can you get the salt back? Yes, if you heat the water. The water goes into the air, and the salt is left in the cup.

Changes you can undo. The word undo has two parts: un means the opposite, and do is the action. For my experiment, I wrote a note: "Experiment: What happens to the ice?" The equipment was simple: a plastic cup, some ice, a digital thermometer, and a plate. First, the ice was put in the cup. Then the cup was put on the plate in the sun. Next, the temperature was checked every ten minutes. After thirty minutes, the ice changed to water. When water is made very cold, it changes back to ice. The ice and the water are the same material, so this change goes both ways.

Changes you cannot undo. Some changes go only one way. Bread is grilled, and toast is made. Toast is a new material, so it cannot change back to bread. A cake is baked in the oven, and it cannot change back to eggs and sugar. Here is my rule: if you get the same material back, the change can go back.

That is the end of my notes. I will read them again on Tuesday evening, after the math test. My room is a mixture, too, with books, socks, and toys on the floor. I cannot undo it before Wednesday! Good luck, Explorers!
